summary: Microsoft's Monster Truck Madness line, covering Terminal Reality's Windows monster-truck racers, the Nintendo 64 port published by Rockstar, and the later THQ/Tantalus Game Boy Advance continuation.

entries.title: Monster Truck Madness

emulation.notes: Use a Windows compatibility or VM route for the original PC release; keep legacy DirectPlay expectations in mind for multiplayer.

primary.why: The original Monster Truck Madness was developed for Microsoft Windows and is the only sourced release, with licensed trucks, drag/circuit/rally/tournament modes, garage tuning, replays, and modem/LAN/TCP/IP multiplayer.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows 95/Windows PC release on period hardware or a compatibility/VM setup; preserve the original DirectPlay-era multiplayer and Direct3D/force-feedback PC presentation where possible.

all_releases.fidelity: Original Windows release with PC graphics options, Direct3D-era acceleration support, and the full mode set.
all_releases.reason: primary: only sourced release and the complete original route.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: No other sourced platform release exists.

entries.remaster_caveats: No sourced remaster or complete edition.

entries.title: Monster Truck Madness 2 / Monster Truck Madness 64

emulation.notes: Use Windows compatibility/VM for the primary PC version; emulate the N64 version only for its console-specific presentation.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Windows PC route for main play, N64 emulation for secondary content

primary.why: Monster Truck Madness 2 launched first on Windows with improved graphics, more trucks and tracks, variable weather, online multiplayer, and compatibility with many custom trucks/tracks. The Nintendo 64 version was a later port released as Monster Truck Madness 64, so Windows is the highest-fidelity and most extensible main route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release on a compatibility/VM setup for the original PC feature set and community-content potential; use the Nintendo 64 version separately only for its console-specific multiplayer adaptation.

secondary.exclusive_content: Monster Truck Madness 64 console adaptation, with local console multiplayer/battle-style modes and Rockstar/WCW presentation distinct from the Windows online-focused release.
secondary.what_to_play: Sample the N64 version's local multiplayer/battle modes and console-specific presentation rather than replaying the full campaign.
secondary.why: The N64 version was released under a distinct title with its own console-specific modes/presentation, but the Windows version remains the best main playthrough.

all_releases.fidelity: Original PC sequel with improved engine, more trucks/tracks, online multiplayer, and community-content compatibility.
all_releases.reason: primary: highest-fidelity and most extensible route.

all_releases.fidelity: Console port released as Monster Truck Madness 64, developed by Edge of Reality and published by Rockstar Games.
all_releases.reason: secondary: preserve the distinct N64 console adaptation, especially local multiplayer/battle-style presentation.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Windows is the higher-fidelity and more extensible primary route, while the Nintendo 64 port is a distinct console adaptation worth sampling for local multiplayer/battle-style presentation.

entries.remaster_caveats: No sourced remaster or complete edition; the N64 release is a port/renamed console adaptation rather than a remaster.

entries.title: Monster Truck Madness

emulation.notes: Use mGBA for clean capture and scaling, or original GBA hardware for authentic handheld play.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Game Boy Advance fidelity with emulator scaling

primary.why: The 2003 Monster Truck Madness was a Game Boy Advance continuation developed by Tantalus and published by THQ, with 2.5D/3D-style handheld racing, powerups, and time-trial play; the GBA cartridge is the only sourced release.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Game Boy Advance version on original hardware or mGBA; use emulator scaling for capture while preserving the handheld frame pacing.

all_releases.fidelity: Handheld 2.5D/3D-style racing release with powerups and time-trial play.
all_releases.reason: primary: only sourced release and the complete handheld route.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: No other sourced platform release exists.

entries.remaster_caveats: No sourced remaster or complete edition.
